summary: In a military barracks, Captain Cable meets Ray, who is apparently responsible for soldiers Kilgore and Rodriguez, and speaks with him about their stored gear and an inconvenience Ray has caused. Cable leads Ray through the barracks, a long low chamber of three-tier sleeping cubicles decorated with personal photos and letters. They find Kilgore and Rodriguez tossing a football and snapping to attention when the captain arrives. The passage is an excerpt from a longer fiction work labeled Book 15, part 93.
one_line: Captain Cable leads Ray through a crowded military barracks to find two soldiers who were goofing off with a football.
key_facts: Captain Cable tells Ray that Ray's soldiers' gear is an inconvenience but Ray will be begging to take it back by tomorrow.
Ray apologizes to Cable for being a dumbass, and Cable responds that he appreciates Ray not pointing out that he is one.
Cable explains that the other soldiers' mates were assigned to pull head polish duty, cleaning the latrine, that morning.
Cable suspects Kilgore and Rodriguez will be nervous because they do not want to be caught lounging when the rest of the barracks troops in.
The barracks is described as a long, low ceilinged chamber divided into neat rows by sleeping cubicles stacked three berths tall.
Ray compares the cubicles to sleeping compartments on passenger trains, with a dark curtain providing the illusion of privacy.
The cubicles are crowded with pictures, letters scrawled in blocky children's handwriting, and fading centerfolds.
Kilgore and Rodriguez are tossing a football in low, tight spirals down the length of the aisle when Cable and Ray arrive.
Rodriguez stands to attention and catches Kilgore's last throw in the middle of his gut without flinching.
Kilgore barks 'Good hands, assclown' at Rodriguez.
Rodriguez answers 'Officer on the deck' with only the slightest hint of strain in his voice.
Cable tells Ray that the two soldiers are on their best behavior at the moment and that it is all downhill from here.
Kilgore snaps off a regulation salute for the captain and begins to apologize for the Deck Officer's pardon.
